subject: Genetics
title: Hemophilia and Royalty
description: A 60-second lesson on Hemophilia and Royalty.

hook.text: Queen Victoria carried a hemophilia gene. She passed it to royal families across Europe. Blood wouldn't clot.

buildup.text: Hemophilia is X-linked recessive. Victoria was a carrier. Her son Leopold died from it. Several grandsons did too.

discovery.text: Through royal marriages, the allele spread to Spain, Germany, and Russia. Alexei, Russia's heir, had hemophilia.

twist.text: Rasputin gained power by appearing to ease Alexei's symptoms. A genetic disease may have changed Russian history.

climax.text: The mutation likely arose spontaneously in Victoria herself. One random error in one queen reshaped a continent.

punchline.text: One mutation in one queen. A continent of consequences.

quiz.question: How did hemophilia spread through European royalty?
